reviews.text: I brought my cat in for an emergency after 3 AM. The service was incredibly thorough. They were kind even on the phone. I was surprised to see how at ease my cat seemed to be by the doctor's care. The explanations were easy to understand, all my concerns were addressed, and I was so glad I brought my cat in. I wish they were my regular vet.

I called late at night because my dog ​​had vomited and I was hesitant about bringing him in. They listened to my details, but then flatly told me they couldn't accept him because they were dealing with an emergency. If that's the case, why did they even ask for details?

As others have written, the reception staff's attitude is terrible. Do they have no compassion for animals?

My pet was diagnosed in the emergency room after ingesting a foreign object, but the attitude of the nurse from the moment we entered the hospital, and then the attitude of the doctor who came out afterward, were truly awful and quite heartless.
I apologize for not having an appointment, but the nurse spoke in a harsh tone, saying, "Time? I can't tell you."
The way the doctor spoke on the phone with another patient was also very cold and harsh.
When the doctor asked questions to confirm the situation, and I specifically mentioned that my pet was lethargic, he said in a way that was overwhelming, "Is that all? At that size, I think it will pass through in the stool."
Seeing my pet lethargic and in pain, I was truly worried and desperately wanted to do something to help, but they didn't consider my feelings at all. It was the worst hospital I've ever been to.
I regret taking my precious family member to such a hospital.
I will never go there again, and I would not recommend it.
Only the nurse who came out last had a kind tone, but the first nurse and doctor seemed to have no heart at all.
I am filled with deep disappointment.

No English assistance and flatly refused to assist with a dying hamster late at night when other clinics were closed. The refusal seemed to be because they don’t handle small pets like that. A veterinarian with medicine, tools, and experience is better than no one; but they didn’t seem to care.

When I got home, I found my dog ​​had eaten chocolate. I frantically called an emergency hospital, but they refused to accept him without even asking for details or the reason.

So, I went to another 24-hour hospital, and on my way, I passed by the hospital I had been told was empty.

Of course, I understand that hospitals have their own reasons for accepting patients, but I find it questionable that they refused without even asking about the situation. If they call themselves an emergency hospital, I would have expected them to at least check the symptoms and the urgency of the situation before treating my dog.

It was a very disappointing response, especially considering the anxiety I felt about my dog's potentially life-threatening situation.
Even after paying a high price for the test, they say there's no way to know anything and then charge me for two days. Please stop.

My beloved cat was cared for in December. He had been listless for a few days, so I took him to the hospital overnight for an X-ray and ultrasound, which diagnosed him as having possibly eaten a toy. His explanations were very kind and easy to understand, and he also arranged hospitalization and surgery. Dr. Shimizu, who was in charge overnight, Dr. Ikeya, who performed the surgery and cared for him afterwards, and all the nurses were very calm, kind, and extremely helpful. I felt at ease as everyone loved him during his hospital stay. I am truly grateful that you saved his life. Thank you so much.

My dog ​​ate something he shouldn't have, and since our regular vet was closed, we went to this hospital. However, the receptionist nurse was incredibly unhelpful, and despite calling itself an emergency clinic, it's strictly by appointment only, so they basically won't see you. The bill was also exorbitant; they said it would cost around 150,000 yen because they needed to do an endoscopy and blood tests, and asked if we were sure we could handle it. I will never go there again, and no matter how desperate you are, you should absolutely avoid this hospital. Thankfully, my dog ​​received proper treatment at another hospital and is now completely recovered. I'm so glad I didn't rush to this hospital.

I had a CT scan here a few months ago, and was told there were no abnormalities.

I sought a second opinion at another hospital, where they reviewed the images from this scan. They said the images were too blurry to detect any abnormalities, and that I should have another proper scan.

I'm very upset that I paid such a high price for the scan, only to find it was largely meaningless.
I used their emergency services when my cat swallowed a foreign object.

My 11-year-old miniature dachshund underwent emergency surgery for a ruptured bladder and received excellent care. It's been two months since discharge, and the scars from the more than 20 stitches have almost completely disappeared. Seeing him running around happily fills me with gratitude to the doctor. Currently, he has no problems with urination or defecation, and since the damage extended to the kidneys and urethra, I believe it's thanks to the meticulous surgery performed to avoid damaging essential tissues.

The accident occurred while traveling, and despite explaining the situation, the local doctor refused to perform any tests, saying he was fine because he could walk. After returning to Tokyo, our regular vet couldn't determine the cause. We were then referred to this hospital, and the emergency surgery was performed just hours after our visit. I believe if we had waited a few more hours, it would have been too late.

Unlike general animal hospitals, this is an emergency hospital with several young doctors who handle major surgeries.

The female doctor in charge listened carefully to the owner's concerns, and her explanations of the diagnosis, treatment plan, and costs were clear. Furthermore, her experience in surgery gave me a sense of reassurance.

Visiting hours are available daily, with ample time slots in the morning and afternoon. The hospital room was right next to the nurses' station, and since other patients were also hospitalized in separate cages in a large ward, visiting hours were limited to 15 minutes per family, with a maximum of two people. With permission, we could bring in food and treats. (Hospital meals were also provided.)
The reception staff and nurses were very friendly and kind whenever we visited. It was also helpful that there was a designated parking lot nearby and we could get a parking ticket at the reception.
Even with a ruptured organ, the dog was still walking and didn't bark loudly. I'm so glad we didn't wait and instead went to this hospital.

The X-rays you took were incredibly clear, unlike anything I'd ever seen before, and I was truly impressed by your technical skill.
Based on the test results, you gave me a very clear explanation, which allowed me to confidently decide on a treatment plan.
My cat, who had been examined and treated, unfortunately passed away, and I had to cancel the appointment. However, you called me afterward and were incredibly kind and helpful. I am truly grateful.

My dog ​​ate a chicken bone, so I called ahead to check, and then went to the hospital that night. They even gave me a rough estimate of the costs over the phone. There aren't any hospitals nearby that have an endoscope, so I went there first.

They explained several methods and the risks of each clearly and carefully. In the end, they were able to remove the bone without using an endoscope. Even then, they checked the X-rays to make sure no bones remained in the stomach, and their explanation of the procedure was very clear and helpful.

The veterinarians have a calm atmosphere and are kind and thorough in their examinations and explanations, so I trust them very much. There are also many kind nurses, so I feel comfortable leaving my seriously ill pet with them.
However, recently I've been troubled by the harshness of one nurse. She started treating me around spring 2025, and her loud voice and overbearing manner make me feel depressed every time. Although it's not directly related to examinations or prescriptions, it makes me feel depressed. I hope things improve soon.

My cat was clearly not well, but my regular vet was closed and I couldn't get in touch with them. I called other vets but they were closed and didn't answer. I called here for help, but they refused to see me. After that, my cat started breathing heavily through its mouth, its eyes wide open, and it struggled in agony before passing away. I'm so upset that they refused to see it without even examining it.

Last night, my cat likely swallowed a toy string (30-40cm), so I called and they said they could help, and I immediately took a taxi there.

They gave me an estimated cost over the phone, so although it was expensive because it was nighttime, I was somewhat prepared, which was good.

Upon arrival, I filled out a questionnaire, and then they examined my cat, performed an ultrasound and X-ray, and said they would induce vomiting (and if she didn't vomit, perform endoscopic surgery). My cat was taken away for the procedure.

I waited anxiously for an hour without any contact, but the doctor arrived and informed me that the vomiting procedure hadn't worked and that there was a high risk of endoscopic surgery because her dinner was stuck in her stomach.

They carefully explained the pros and cons of the procedure, listing them by hand on a piece of paper, which was very reassuring.

Ultimately, no further treatment was performed, and I was scheduled to see my regular vet the next morning. They shared the information with my regular vet via fax, and even provided the X-ray and ultrasound results on a CD. They handled everything very professionally. I took him to our regular vet first thing in the morning, and they tried to induce vomiting again, but he still wouldn't vomit. They ended up performing endoscopic surgery, and thankfully, the 30cm string was successfully removed.

It was my first time going there on short notice, but this veterinarian is extremely trustworthy.

Thank you so much.

Despite it being an emergency, I was told they couldn't see me and I should try somewhere else.

What's the point of an emergency hospital? I will never contact them again.

I'm not sure if she's a nurse or an office worker at the front desk, but she's wearing pink slabs and glasses. She's beyond unfriendly. I introduced myself as "Nice to meet you, I'm the XX who called earlier," but she ignored me. Surely she could at least say hello? I came to the hospital during an emergency and feeling anxious, but she didn't even offer a word of sympathy. It's practically confrontational. Even though the ER consultation fee is high, I think that kind of behavior is rude to patients. She kept asking me all sorts of questions over the phone, and if she can't handle it, she should have just said no. My regular doctor is on vacation, so I'm rushing around calling around to find other places that can help me. I guess she has no intention of changing her mind, despite what other reviews have said. I don't think there's anything wrong with the doctor.

My puppy suddenly started vomiting violently and repeatedly at night and became lethargic, so I called this emergency center, which my regular vet had recommended as a backup in case of an emergency.

During the initial phone consultation, they carefully explained the key points for monitoring the puppy's condition. Since I was still unsure about self-diagnosis, I discussed a visit time and had a doctor examine the puppy.

It's a very considerate hospital that provides 24-hour service, even though it's not a public facility.

I was prepared for the high costs of veterinary care, but during the phone consultation, they provided an estimate of the expected treatment and cost (of course, this could change significantly depending on the diagnosis), which was very reassuring.

Even though it was the middle of the night, they provided a thorough diagnosis and thoughtful advice on how to raise the puppy, which was incredibly helpful.

Despite advertising 24-hour emergency care, it seems to be strictly by appointment only, so don't be fooled!

I don't even want to give it one star.

I went there urgently needing treatment, but they told me it was by appointment only and seemed quite annoyed.

When I asked if there was a night emergency nearby, they laughed and told me to "look it up myself."

They said they could administer an emetic, but it would cost 55,000 yen.

Furthermore, they said they couldn't perform any further treatment or examination (apparently they were performing emergency surgery at the time). Even so, I asked for advice because I'm not sure if I should get the emetic immediately, but they just said, "Decide for yourself."

They laughed mockingly at this point as well.

When I said I would look up a night emergency nearby, they asked, "Do you know how long it will take before they do it or not?"

How would I know that?

The person handling my case seemed to be going back inside, so I asked what I should do if I wanted the treatment, and they said, "I'll come back." I looked for a place to go for about 10 minutes and left, but they never came back during that time.

I'm absolutely furious that you're trying to kill my family.

What responsibility will you take if something irreversible happened during the time it took to get here and during this awful exchange?

It's been a long time since I've seen someone so cold and contemptuous.
My cat was saved from a critical condition due to acute renal failure.

The staff member who is often at the reception desk and answers reservation calls is a woman with glasses, a pink outfit, and pink hair.

She is extremely unfriendly and has a bad attitude.

We are so grateful to the doctor who treated our dog!! They saved his life.

Our dog is a 4-year-6-month-old Miniature Dachshund.

Initially, he was diagnosed with a herniated disc at our local vet. His hind legs became increasingly weak, and his condition worsened. We were scheduled for a follow-up appointment after a week of steroid medication, but we became worried. Three days later, we sought a second opinion at a different hospital, not our regular vet. They determined it was an emergency and referred us to the well-equipped Bunkyo Animal Emergency Center.

First, they performed detailed tests (blood tests, ultrasound, X-rays) to check for the risks of general anesthesia during an MRI and to rule out other illnesses.

Afterward, we received explanations regarding the test results, confirmation of whether we should proceed with the MRI, and signing of the consent form for surgery.

At that time, they also explained the costs of the tests, surgery, and hospitalization.

Since we live far away and the MRI would take some time, they kindly allowed us to consult by phone after returning home.


They kept us informed by phone at every step, including the timing of the anesthesia, the upcoming MRI scan, and the test results.

After the MRI scan, we received confirmation of "myelomalacia."

They explained in detail whether we should proceed with surgery, the possibility of postoperative recovery, and the likely need for lifelong care.

When we requested surgery, the doctor assured us, "We will remove the lesion, no matter how long it takes."

After the surgery, they called us, and we visited again the following day for a postoperative explanation. They explained everything in great detail and patiently answered all our questions.

We visited every day until discharge, and whenever the doctor was available, he would come to see us and tell us about our progress each day.

Even when the doctor was unable to come due to surgery, he would call us.

On the day of discharge, even though it was his day off, the doctor came out to accommodate our schedule.

Afterward, they continued to answer our questions and address our concerns by phone.

As others have mentioned, the cost is indeed high.

The detailed examination cost 60,000 yen, and the MRI, surgery, and hospitalization fees came to approximately 600,000 yen.
Before coming to this hospital, we had been given a rough estimate of the costs by the referring hospital, so we agreed to the consultation.
However, our life was saved.
Although there will be paralysis in the lower body, we agreed to this during the detailed explanation before the surgery.

The doctor in charge was truly knowledgeable and trustworthy, which is why we were able to entrust the surgery to him.

Thank you so much for saving our life.

Addendum 2024/8/6
The doctor in charge called us directly to ask about our progress and if we had any questions.

We never expected such aftercare, so we are truly grateful.

We asked many questions and talked for a long time, but he answered each one very carefully.

Finally, he said, "This is not the end, so please feel free to contact us anytime if you have any problems or concerns."

Afterwards, I took advantage of their kind offer and called them because there was something I had forgotten to ask, and they handled that call very courteously as well.

I am truly grateful.

The phone call I received was unpleasant.
I was told that there was only one veterinarian treating the seriously ill animal and that I should try someone else.
They explained everything very carefully, which made me feel very relieved and at ease. If it were closer, I would like to go there even outside of emergencies.

They helped us in an emergency situation, discovered a heart condition (right atrial angiosarcoma), and, regarding the liver issue that our previous vet had mentioned, it matched the location of a previous liver abscess (I had brought an ultrasound image of the liver abscess so they could compare the locations), allowing them to determine it wasn't serious. The veterinarian who was in charge that night explained everything thoroughly, including the life-threatening risks during hospitalization, the fact that treatment would take priority, and that they wouldn't be able to call even in critical condition (they fulfilled their duty to explain).

When we returned home after our dog's bravery, almost all the other hospitalized dogs had urinary catheters.

My dog ​​also had a urinary catheter inserted.

The veterinarian in charge that morning looked displeased. Perhaps it was because I asked about the urinary catheter... but almost all the dogs had them, and I wondered if it was just to make toilet management easier? I felt a sense of unease.

After being discharged from the hospital, that evening, my dog ​​had severe blood in his urine...
However, our regular veterinary hospital was slow to treat him, and he died a few days later from pyelonephritis.

I am grateful to ER Nerima for saving his life, but I can't help but wonder if the subsequent pyelonephritis was caused by the urinary tract infection. I want to believe it was just a means to save his life!

If it was pyelonephritis, our regular veterinary hospital should have treated it after taking over, and I want to believe that ER Nerima did their best to save his life.
Due to the busy situation, I was refused an appointment, but the service over the phone was excellent, with the doctor directing me to other affiliated centers and letting me know what was available.

As the name suggests, this is an emergency clinic. If your pet is seriously ill, this is your first choice (referral letter required).
They have multiple doctors and nurses and are open 24 hours a day, so you can rely on them.
(Recently, there's been an increase in veterinary clinics located in apartment buildings, and it seems like the number of clinics where you can go 24 hours a day or have your pet hospitalized, often at the veterinarian's home, is decreasing, as they lack nighttime consultations and hospitalization facilities.)

Animals are important members of the family. Having them treated here will be the best choice for your pet (of course, there are individual differences in cases).

This is an emergency clinic. Have your regular veterinarian contact them in advance.

Please be careful, as an increase in walk-in visits (they may not accept them) could affect other patients. Even in emergencies, it's best to always call first.

Therefore, when choosing a regular veterinarian, be sure to confirm their referral network in case the clinic is unable to handle your pet! (Outside of regular hours, on holidays, for rare diseases, emergencies, hospitalization, etc.)

They may not refer you to specialist hospitals they don't have a relationship with, or if the veterinarian graduated from a different university.
